interest: This file illustrates the State Department's internal recordkeeping and cross-referencing practices for agricultural and industrial intelligence in interwar Japan, demonstrating how administrative docket sheets preserve traces of substantive reporting. The reference to Ambassador W. Cameron Forbes visiting the Imperial stud farm in Hokkaido highlights American diplomatic interest in Japanese horse breeding, an area critical to military logistics, agriculture, and imperial prestige. In addition, the attached wool industry docket entry offers valuable insight into early 1930s Japanese state-guided economic rationalization and cartelization efforts led by the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau in the textile sector.
overview: This file from the U.S. State Department's decimal central files (Record Group 59) consists of 'List of Papers' docket sheets from 1930 relating to Japanese animal husbandry and related industries. The primary sheet for decimal file 894.62211 (covering horses, ponies, mules, asses, and burros in Japan) records an October 31, 1930 entry regarding horse breeding and an official visit by U.S. Ambassador W. Cameron Forbes to the Imperial stud in Hokkaido, cross-referencing Forbes's personnel file (123 Forbes, W. Cameron/52). A second docket sheet bundled with the file concerns sheep, goats, and wool in Japan, recording an August 1, 1930 entry from Edwin L. Neville regarding proposals to rationalize production and sales and amalgamate the woolen industry considered by the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau, cross-referencing decimal file 894.00 P.M./32.

subfiles.summary: This List of Papers docket sheet for decimal file 894.62211 (Horse, pony, mule, ass, burro -- Japan) catalogs records received in 1930 concerning domestic beasts of burden. It contains a single cross-reference entry dated October 31, 1930, regarding Japanese horse breeding and an official visit by American Ambassador W. Cameron Forbes to the Imperial stud in Hokkaido. The note cross-references personnel file 123 Forbes, W. Cameron/52 for the original communication from Ambassador Forbes.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Horse Breeding in Japan (894.62211)

subfiles.about: State Department List of Papers docket sheet indexing an entry on the rationalization and amalgamation of the Japanese woolen industry.
subfiles.summary: This List of Papers docket sheet covers documents concerning sheep, goats, and wool in Japan during 1930. The entry, dated August 1, 1930, cross-references a report from Edwin L. Neville concerning the rationalization of production and sales as well as the proposed fundamental rationalization by amalgamation of the wool industry. These plans were discussed at the July 1930 meeting of the woolen industry committee of the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau, with the original despatch filed under 894.00 P.M./32.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Rationalization of the Japanese Wool Industry
